ELIAS.name: Elias Voss
ELIAS.locked_look: 70s, gaunt face with deep nasolabial folds, thinning silver hair combed to the side, wiry frame. Wears a charcoal wool cardigan over a cream cotton henley, dark brown corduroy trousers, and worn leather apron. Silver-rimmed magnifying loupe hangs around his neck on a braided cord. Hands are long-fingered, spotted with age, stained faintly with oil.

visual_style: Warm tungsten practical light washes against cold blue rain-slicked darkness, shallow depth of field on close treatments, grainy 35mm texture reminiscent of late-era Kieslowski naturalism.

scenes.location: Antique clock repair workshop — interior, night
scenes.shot_purpose_summary: Establish the cramped, artifact-filled workshop and the lonely figure of Elias beneath a pool of warm lamplight, rain visible against the window.

shots.action_beat: A wide static shot reveals a cluttered workshop crammed with shelves of disassembled clocks, brass gears, and tools. A single amber desk lamp sits center frame. Rain streaks diagonally across a tall arched window on the right. ELIAS, bent over his workbench, is a small dark shape against the warm light pool.
shots.ambience: Low, cavernous workshop bed: a chorus of mismatched clock ticks at varying tempos, rain hissing softly against the tall arched window, distant hum of late-night city traffic three blocks away, occasional low creak of old timber settling
shots.sfx: Rain drumming diagonally against glass, irregular clock ticks from a dozen unmastered timepieces, the faint groan of a pendulum swinging somewhere off-frame, a metal tool clinking softly as Elias shifts his weight
shots.score: Near-silent — a barely perceptible, dissonant drone underneath, like a single cello harmonic bowed too long, evoking isolation and suspended time

shots.action_beat: The camera slowly pushes toward Elias from across the room. He is hunched over the workbench, back partially to us, one hand holding a brass pendulum steady while the other adjusts a screw with tweezers. Raindrops race down the window behind him.
shots.ambience: Low, cavernous workshop bed: a chorus of mismatched clock ticks at varying tempos, rain hissing softly against the tall arched window, distant hum of late-night city traffic three blocks away, occasional low creak of old timber settling
shots.sfx: Brass pendulum being held still — a soft metallic resistance sound, tweezers scraping against a tiny screw head, raindrops racing down the window in rivulets, the whisper of Elias's cardigan sleeve against the workbench cloth, a slow exhale
shots.score: Sparse, single-note piano figures arrive slowly — each note spaced like a heartbeat, minor key, barely above the ambience; a subtle bass swell begins as the push-in progresses

shots.action_beat: Extreme tight on Elias's left eye behind the magnifying loupe. His pupil contracts slightly as he focuses. Rain reflections shimmer in the curve of the lens. A thin line of sweat traces from his temple into his collar. He blinks once, slowly.
shots.ambience: Low, cavernous workshop bed: a chorus of mismatched clock ticks at varying tempos, rain hissing softly against the tall arched window, distant hum of late-night city traffic three blocks away, occasional low creak of old timber settling
shots.sfx: The wet blink — a soft, intimate eyelid parting sound; the faintest shift of breath against the loupe glass; a distant thunder roll muffled by the building; the rain reflections on the lens produce almost a shimmering audio texture — a high, delicate metallic tinkle no more than a whisper
shots.score: Solo viola enters — a single sustained note with slight vibrato, mournful and narrow in range; it holds without resolution, mirroring the static, unblinking focus of the shot

shots.action_beat: Over Elias's right shoulder, the frame fills with the open face of the antique clock on the workbench — exposed mainspring, brass cogs, and a cracked porcelain dial. His oil-stained fingers move deliberately between components.
shots.ambience: Low, cavernous workshop bed: a chorus of mismatched clock ticks at varying tempos, rain hissing softly against the tall arched window, distant hum of late-night city traffic three blocks away, occasional low creak of old timber settling
shots.sfx: Oil-stained fingertips brushing against brass cogs — a dry, granular friction; the mainspring's faint tension hum; a gear tooth clicking against another as fingers reposition it; the soft dab of the oil brush approaching from edge of frame
shots.score: The viola note fractures into a tremolo — short, nervous bows suggesting precision under pressure; a muted guitar plucks a recurring three-note figure, mechanical yet human

scenes.shot_purpose_summary: Elias works deeper into the clock mechanism; a gear refuses to seat and he applies oil with a fine brush, his movements growing more precise and deliberate.

shots.action_beat: Wide establishing from the same position as Scene 1's opening — the cluttered workshop bathed in amber lamplight, rain still streaking the tall arched window on the right. ELIAS is at the workbench, leaning closer to the clock, his charcoal cardigan and leather apron visible. The composition mirrors Scene 1's master, grounding us in the same geography before the scene progresses.
shots.ambience: Low, cavernous workshop bed: a chorus of mismatched clock ticks at varying tempos, rain hissing softly against the tall arched window, distant hum of late-night city traffic three blocks away, occasional low creak of old timber settling
shots.sfx: Rain continues its diagonal streak against glass; the clock on the workbench emits a stronger, more singular tick than the surrounding cacophony — as if it has become the anchor in the room's temporal chaos; Elias's leather apron creaks as he adjusts his stance
shots.score: Returns to the near-silence of the first scene's master — the dissonant cello drone re-enters, but slightly warmer now, a half-step lower, suggesting accumulated focus

shots.action_beat: Medium shot from the side. Elias threads a tiny brass pinion into the clock's interior. He tests the engagement — the gear slips free. He exhales through his nose, sets it down, and reaches for a different tool on the cloth-spattered bench. Camera remains on the same side of the 180-axis as Scene 1 (right of the bench), maintaining consistent screen direction.
shots.ambience: Low, cavernous workshop bed: a chorus of mismatched clock ticks at varying tempos, rain hissing softly against the tall arched window, distant hum of late-night city traffic three blocks away, occasional low creak of old timber settling
shots.sfx: Tiny brass pinion being guided through a aperture — a soft metallic whisper; the gear slips free with a frustrated tick-tick; a wet exhalation through the nose; the pinion set down on the cloth with a faint clatter; fingers scraping across the cloth-spattered bench searching, then grasping a different tool — a soft metallic snick
shots.score: A brief dissonance — the piano plays a wrong note, then corrects; the viola responds with a questioning downward slide, as if echoing Elias's own frustration

shots.action_beat: Low angle close on Elias's hands. His thumb and forefinger hold a slender oil brush. He dips it into a ceramic dish of watch oil and carefully applies a single glistening drop to the escapement pivot. His hand does not tremble.
shots.ambience: Low, cavernous workshop bed: a chorus of mismatched clock ticks at varying tempos, rain hissing softly against the tall arched window, distant hum of late-night city traffic three blocks away, occasional low creak of old timber settling
shots.sfx: The oil brush dipping — a wet, sticky pull from ceramic; the brush tip meeting brass — a glistening, almost viscous contact sound; the single drop of oil landing on the escapement pivot with a micro-micro click; the steadiness of the hand produces no extraneous movement sounds — only the deliberate, confident touch
shots.score: The music drops out almost entirely for two seconds, leaving only ambience and sfx — then a solo clarinet enters, clean and warm, playing a simple ascending phrase that mirrors the precision of the oil application; the hand's steadiness gives the music a sense of reverence

shots.action_beat: Over Elias's right shoulder again, maintaining the same shoulder and axis established in Scene 1's OTS. The gear now catches and turns smoothly. The second hand on the clock face gives a tentative tick forward — then stops. Elias reaches for the winding key at the base of the clock.
shots.ambience: Low, cavernous workshop bed: a chorus of mismatched clock ticks at varying tempos, rain hissing softly against the tall arched window, distant hum of late-night city traffic three blocks away, occasional low creak of old timber settling
shots.sfx: The gear catches — a clean, satisfying metallic engagement; the clock's second hand begins its tentative ticking forward, one click per second, faltering; it stops with a final, dead tick; Elias's fingers reach for the winding key — leather and metal friction; the key turning in the winding hole with a series of firm, rhythmic clicks
shots.score: The ticking of the clock itself becomes percussive under the score — each tick accenting a brushed snare hit, sparse and ghostly; the clarinet re-enters, now joined by a solo flute playing in counterpoint, both instruments suggesting fragile hope

shots.action_beat: High angle looking down at Elias leaning over the clock. He sets the key down and presses his palm flat against the clock's wooden case, listening. The camera tilts up slowly to his face — his eyes are half-closed, listening intently. His silver-rimmed loupe still hangs around his neck, catching the amber light.
shots.ambience: Low, cavernous workshop bed: a chorus of mismatched clock ticks at varying tempos, rain hissing softly against the tall arched window, distant hum of late-night city traffic three blocks away, occasional low creak of old timber settling
shots.sfx: The winding key set down on the bench — a solid, final click; Elias's palm pressing against the wooden clock case — a soft thud of flesh on varnished oak; the clock ticking grows subtly louder in the mix, as if heard through the wood and into his body; the loupe around his neck catches and produces a tiny glassy ping as it brushes his collarbone
shots.score: The tilt-up from hands to face coincides with a swelling of strings — cello and viola together, warm and expansive but restrained; the music opens like a breath Elias has been holding; a single high violin harmonic appears near the top of the tilt, catching the amber light sonically

scenes.shot_purpose_summary: The ticking clock reveals a hidden compartment. Elias pries it open and discovers a yellowed folded note inside.

shots.action_beat: Wide establishing matching the composition of the previous scenes' opens — same workshop geography, amber lamp pool, rain on the right window. ELIAS is now leaning very close to the back of the clock, one hand braced on the casing, the loupe swinging slightly from his neck. The shot holds for a beat before he begins running his fingertips along the rear panel.
shots.ambience: Low, cavernous workshop bed: a chorus of mismatched clock ticks at varying tempos, rain hissing softly against the tall arched window, distant hum of late-night city traffic three blocks away, occasional low creak of old timber settling
shots.sfx: The clock's tick has grown more assertive — it is no longer competing with the other clocks but commanding attention; the loupe swings gently from Elias's neck, producing tiny glassy clicks against his collarbone; the beat of silence before he begins searching is palpable — only rain and tick; his fingertips begin dragging across walnut wood — a dry, searching scratch
shots.score: A low, pulsing synth pad enters — not electronic in texture but organic, like a bowed vibraphone played extremely slowly; it pulses in time with the clock tick, creating an uncanny sense of synchronization between mechanism and mood

shots.action_beat: Handheld medium follows Elias as he leans closer to the clock, squinting at the back panel. The ticking is louder now — steady, rhythmic. He runs his fingertips along the edge of the walnut casing, feeling for irregularities. Camera stays on the same side of the axis (right of bench), preserving screen direction.
shots.ambience: Low, cavernous workshop bed: a chorus of mismatched clock ticks at varying tempos, rain hissing softly against the tall arched window, distant hum of late-night city traffic three blocks away, occasional low creak of old timber settling
shots.sfx: Handheld camera movement adds a subtle fabric rustle — Elias's cardigan and the leather apron shifting; his squint produces nothing audible but his breath quickens imperceptibly; the ticking grows louder in the mix with each frame, as if the camera is leaning in sonically too; fingertips tracing the walnut edge — dry, precise, searching scratches; a soft inhale as he feels something
shots.score: The pulsing vibraphone-like pad intensifies slightly; a prepared piano enters — notes struck with felt hammers, producing soft, muffled tones that mirror the tactile searching; the music doesn't yet know what it's looking for either

shots.action_beat: Low angle insert on Elias's fingers finding a nearly invisible seam along the rear panel. He presses a small brass button disguised as a knot in the wood. A soft click echoes. A thin rectangular compartment door springs outward a quarter-inch.
shots.ambience: Low, cavernous workshop bed: a chorus of mismatched clock ticks at varying tempos, rain hissing softly against the tall arched window, distant hum of late-night city traffic three blocks away, occasional low creak of old timber settling
shots.sfx: Fingertips parting the nearly invisible seam — a whisper of wood fibers separating; the press against the disguised brass button — a solid, resonant CLICK that rings slightly louder than it should, as if the clock itself approves; the compartment door springs outward with a sharp, well-oiled SNICK, followed by the faintest hiss of displaced air from within the sealed cavity
shots.score: Everything cuts for a fraction of a second — then a single, bright glockenspiel note strikes, pure and surprised, hanging in the air; the vibraphone pad returns, now in a higher register, shimmering with wonder rather than tension

shots.action_beat: Close up on the opened compartment. Inside, wrapped in faded waxed paper, is a narrow folded note. Elias's stained fingers reach in, lift the paper bundle, and begin to unwrap it. The push-in slows as the paper falls away to reveal yellowed paper with dark cursive handwriting.
shots.ambience: Low, cavernous workshop bed: a chorus of mismatched clock ticks at varying tempos, rain hissing softly against the tall arched window, distant hum of late-night city traffic three blocks away, occasional low creak of old timber settling
shots.sfx: Stained fingers reaching into the compartment — a soft brush against aged wood; the waxed paper bundle being lifted — a dry, brittle rustle, paper older than the clock itself; the unwrapping produces a succession of delicate cracks and folds, each one whispered; as the paper falls away, the reveal is almost silent — only the faintest sigh of paper settling onto the workbench
shots.score: The glockenspiel note blooms into a full but restrained string phrase — strings playing sul tasto, bows close to the fingerboard, creating a veiled, dreamlike warmth; a solo oboe weaves through the strings with a melody that feels like recognition, like something long-awaited finally arriving

shots.action_beat: Extreme close-up over Elias's right shoulder — consistent with all prior OTS shots. The note fills most of the frame. The ink reads in flowing script: 'For the one who finds this — the time was never the problem.' The edges of the paper are frayed and browned. One tear mark runs through the lower right corner. Elias's oil-stained thumb holds the edge of the paper steady.
shots.dialogue: ELIAS (a whisper, almost inaudible, reading aloud): 'For the one who finds this...' [beat] 'The time was never the problem.'
shots.ambience: Low, cavernous workshop bed: a chorus of mismatched clock ticks at varying tempos, rain hissing softly against the tall arched window, distant hum of late-night city traffic three blocks away, occasional low creak of old timber settling
shots.sfx: Elias's oil-stained thumb holding the paper steady — the faintest fabric and paper friction; his breath hitches almost imperceptibly on the reading; the paper's frayed edges produce a barely audible whisper as his thumb shifts; in the background, all the other clocks in the workshop seem to fall silent for a moment — only the one repaired clock continues its steady tick, as if it alone was meant to deliver this message
shots.score: The string phrase resolves to a sustained, open chord — major but with an added sixth that keeps it from being sentimental; the oboe holds a single long note that slowly fades; the rain continues its quiet percussion outside; the ticking clock remains the only metronomic presence — the one thing that was always right all along

locations.name: Watchmaker's Workshop
locations.locked_look: Cramped Victorian-era workshop crammed with towering shelves of brass gears, half-dismantled clocks, and leather tool rolls. Warm amber lamplight pools over a scarred oak workbench. Dark rain-streaked window to one side. Everything coated in fine golden dust.

props.locked_look: an ornate antique clock with a dark wood casing, brass pendulum, and Roman numeral face, showing visible signs of age and wear
